trained_on: TRAIN split (15 samples, 1 positive), using leave-one-out OUT-OF-FOLD ML probabilities (never in-sample)
critical_finding: The coefficient on oof_ml_probability_svm is NEGATIVE (-1.1468), i.e. inverted relative to the intuitive expectation that a higher ML score should increase fused vulnerability probability. Root cause: leave-one-out CV on a training set with exactly 1 positive example produces a STRUCTURALLY DEGENERATE out-of-fold value for that one positive (its held-out fold contains zero positives to train on, so its OOF score is fixed at the negative-class floor, 0.0) -- the lowest ML score in the entire training set is attached to the only positive label. A logistic regression fit on this single, structurally-forced data point learns an inverted coefficient. This is reported as direct evidence that OOF-based fusion training is not statistically meaningful with only 1 positive training example, not as a defect in the fusion methodology itself.
